event: Mission San Diego de Alcalá founded; Spanish occupation of Alta California begins
why_it_matters: Begins the mission-presidio-pueblo system: California's first apparatus of labour and record.

event: Mission San Francisco de Asís founded at what is now 320 Dolores Street
why_it_matters: Anchors the Spanish claim to the Pacific's greatest natural harbour. Oldest intact building in the city.

event: Mexican independence; Alta California transfers to Mexico
why_it_matters: Territory transferred without administrative capacity; land grants replace governance.

event: Secularisation of the missions begins
why_it_matters: Largest land transfer in California history. Restitution promised to neophytes; almost none delivered.

event: Gold discovered at Sutter's Mill
why_it_matters: Detonates the incentive structure of the Pacific coast. Marshall and Sutter both ruined by it.

event: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo cedes California to the United States
why_it_matters: Converts occupation into legal ownership. Signed nine days after the gold discovery, in ignorance of it.

event: California constitution signed at Colton Hall
why_it_matters: Statehood organised without congressional authorisation; slavery prohibited.

event: Foreign Miners' Tax enacted
why_it_matters: Extraction from Mexican, Chilean and Peruvian miners. First appearance of a recurring Californian manoeuvre.

event: Act for the Government and Protection of Indians
why_it_matters: Permits arrest of Indians deemed loitering and indenture of Indigenous children. Forced labour in a free state.

event: California admitted as a state under the Compromise of 1850
why_it_matters: Places California on the sectional chessboard from its first day, which decides the railroad route in 1862.

event: California Land Act establishes the land commission
why_it_matters: Places burden of proof on Mexican grant-holders. Transfers land by procedure rather than by seizure.

event: Congress appropriates $150,000 for Pacific railroad surveys
actors: US Congress; Jefferson Davis (Secretary of War)
why_it_matters: Four corridors surveyed. Every field commander reports his own route is best; Congress cannot decide.

event: Gadsden Purchase signed
why_it_matters: Acquires the strip required for a 32nd-parallel southern railroad route.

event: Jefferson Davis speaks for a transcontinental railroad days before leaving the Senate
why_it_matters: 'To couple with bonds of iron the people of the Pacific with the valley of the Mississippi.' His departure is what makes it possible.

event: Central Pacific Railroad incorporated
actors: Leland Stanford; Collis Huntington; Mark Hopkins; Charles Crocker; Theodore Judah
why_it_matters: Four merchants and an engineer. Judah is bought out and dies in 1863.

event: Pacific Railway Act signed
why_it_matters: Passes only after secession empties the Southern seats. Land grants and 30-year bonds at 6 per cent. Union Pacific is the first federally chartered corporation since the Second Bank.

event: Chinese workers strike on the Sierra grade
actors: Central Pacific Chinese workforce; Charles Crocker
why_it_matters: Several thousand men demand pay parity and shorter tunnel hours. Broken within a week by cutting off food.

event: Golden spike completes the transcontinental railroad
why_it_matters: A public work becomes a private monopoly. The Chinese workforce is absent from the photograph.

event: Southern Pacific completes the line to Los Angeles
why_it_matters: Consolidation of rail power; the company begins deciding which towns exist.

event: Mussel Slough shootout
why_it_matters: Seven dead in a dispute over railroad land titles. The physical edge of legal architecture.

event: Chinese Exclusion Act signed
why_it_matters: First federal law barring a nationality. The men who built the Sierra grade are prohibited from the country they connected.

event: Leland Stanford Jr. dies in Florence
why_it_matters: The university follows. Corrects the 1885 date given in some drafts.

event: Stanford Founding Grant executed
why_it_matters: Self-perpetuating board, insulated from politics, endowed with land that cannot be sold. The clause that produces the research park in 1951.

event: Santa Clara County v. Southern Pacific decided
why_it_matters: Decided on narrow grounds; the reporter's headnote records corporate personhood. Doctrine develops over subsequent decades.

event: Yick Wo v. Hopkins decided
why_it_matters: A law fair on its face but administered with an unequal hand violates equal protection. Brought by Chinese laundry operators.

event: Stanford University opens
why_it_matters: Free tuition, coeducational, practical curriculum. First president is a leading eugenicist.

event: Leland Stanford dies during the Panic of 1893
why_it_matters: Estate frozen; the federal government sues for $15 million. The university nearly closes.

event: United States v. Wong Kim Ark decided
why_it_matters: Establishes birthright citizenship, on a case brought by a man born in San Francisco to Chinese parents.

event: Edward Ross forced out of Stanford
actors: Jane Stanford; David Starr Jordan; Edward A. Ross
why_it_matters: Founding controversy of American academic freedom, at a university built by a railroad, over criticism of railroads.

event: Jane Stanford dies in Honolulu
why_it_matters: Cause contested. The institution continues without structural change, which is the load-bearing fact.

event: San Francisco earthquake and fire
why_it_matters: Stanford badly damaged and absorbs it. Assets were land and endowment, not buildings.

event: California sterilisation law enacted
why_it_matters: California performs roughly a third of the recorded US total. Law stands until 1979.

event: California Alien Land Law
why_it_matters: Bars aliens ineligible for citizenship from owning agricultural land; aimed at Japanese farmers.

event: Hoover funds what becomes the Hoover War Collection
why_it_matters: $50,000 and agents in a collapsed Europe. California acquires memory infrastructure.

event: Stanford Graduate School of Business founded
why_it_matters: The management credential formalised. Steinbeck leaves without a degree the same year.

event: Steinbeck's 'The Harvest Gypsies' begins publication
why_it_matters: An administrative record of a labour system compiled by someone with no institutional interest in the outcome.

event: Hewlett-Packard founded at 367 Addison Avenue
actors: Bill Hewlett; David Packard; Frederick Terman
why_it_matters: The garage is real and it is not the explanation. Terman told them to stay.

event: Executive Order 9066
why_it_matters: Incarceration of some 120,000 people of Japanese ancestry. Property lost at distress prices; the transfer had beneficiaries.

event: Vannevar Bush delivers 'Science, the Endless Frontier'
why_it_matters: The intellectual case for permanent federal funding of basic research through universities.

event: Office of Naval Research established
why_it_matters: Fills the five-year gap before the NSF. American basic science funding is architected with a service branch as founding patron.

event: Stanford Research Institute established
why_it_matters: Owned by the university. The ownership is what the 1969 protests turn on.

event: Stanford Industrial Park opens
actors: Frederick Terman; Alf Brandin; Varian Associates
location: Page Mill Road, Palo Alto, CA
why_it_matters: First university-owned industrial park in the US. Direct consequence of the 1885 prohibition on selling land.
note: Sources differ on authorised 1951 vs opened 1953; resolve

event: Lockheed Missiles and Space opens in Sunnyvale
why_it_matters: Becomes the county's largest employer and is absent from the region's origin story.

event: Shockley Semiconductor opens in Mountain View
why_it_matters: Located there because his mother lived there.

event: The eight resign from Shockley; Fairchild Semiconductor follows
actors: Robert Noyce; Gordon Moore; Jean Hoerni; Eugene Kleiner; Arthur Rock; and others
why_it_matters: The spinoff becomes the Valley's reproductive mechanism, enabled by California's refusal to enforce non-competes.

event: Planar process developed at Fairchild
why_it_matters: Makes the integrated circuit manufacturable. The advantage lives in people and therefore walks.

event: Knight secures Tiger distribution rights in Kobe
why_it_matters: Blue Ribbon Sports invented on the spot. The company began as a Stanford class paper.

event: Fairchild opens assembly operations in Hong Kong
why_it_matters: The offshore turn in semiconductors, in the same years Knight is arranging it in footwear.

event: Moore's law published
why_it_matters: A coordination device rather than a prediction. Sets the industry's clock for half a century.

event: Engelbart's demonstration at the Fall Joint Computer Conference
why_it_matters: Mouse, hypertext, windows, collaborative editing. Federally funded and commercially uncaptured.

event: Students occupy the Applied Electronics Laboratory
why_it_matters: Nine days. They print the classified research they find. The senate bans classified work on 24 April.

event: Police tear-gas students protesting the SRI divestment
why_it_matters: They had asked the university to take responsibility. It took its name off the door instead.

event: First ARPANET message, UCLA to SRI
why_it_matters: The system crashes after two letters. The internet's first word is 'lo'.

event: Trustees set terms for the SRI divestment
why_it_matters: SRI sold to itself for 1 per cent of gross revenues up to $25 million. Pressure produced reorganisation, not reform.

event: Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia Capital founded on Sand Hill Road
actors: Eugene Kleiner; Tom Perkins; Don Valentine
why_it_matters: Both founded by operators from the semiconductor industry, four minutes from the campus supplying the deal flow.

event: First Homebrew Computer Club meeting
why_it_matters: Circulating culture, enclosed within about five years.

event: ERISA prudent man rule clarified
why_it_matters: Admits pension money to venture funds. The public-money leg of the capital chokepoint.

event: IBM Personal Computer development; MS-DOS licensed non-exclusively
why_it_matters: The most valuable clause never inserted. Hardware commoditises; the operating system does not.

event: Genentech IPO
why_it_matters: Biology financed like software, on a Stanford and UCSF patent.

event: Bayh-Dole Act enacted
why_it_matters: Universities take title to federally funded inventions. Answers the question Act III left open.

event: NSFNET backbone decommissioned; the network passes to commercial operators
why_it_matters: Thirty years of public investment transferred without compensation, equity, or public debate.

event: Netscape IPO
why_it_matters: Built on Mosaic, developed at a public university on federal funding.

event: Section 230 enacted
why_it_matters: Twenty-six words. The legal foundation of the platform economy.

event: Google incorporated
why_it_matters: Their published paper argues ad-funded search will be biased against users. Stanford owns the PageRank patent.

event: eBay acquires PayPal
why_it_matters: About $1.5 billion. The product was payments; the durable asset was the address book.

event: Amazon Web Services launches
why_it_matters: Computing as a metered utility. Within fifteen years much of the internet runs on three providers.

event: Nvidia introduces CUDA
why_it_matters: A software ecosystem accumulated fifteen years before there was a market for it. The switching cost that holds the position.

event: Facebook acquires Instagram
why_it_matters: About $1 billion for a company with no revenue. Buying the competitor before it is one.

event: Cambridge Analytica reporting published
why_it_matters: The neutrality posture collapses in public.

event: UN fact-finding mission reports on Myanmar
why_it_matters: Addresses the platform's role in the spread of hate speech. The company's own commissioned assessment follows.

event: FTC announces $5 billion Facebook privacy settlement
why_it_matters: Largest privacy penalty the agency had imposed.

event: Proposition 22 passes in California
why_it_matters: Over $200 million spent to exempt platforms from a classification law passed the previous year.

event: CHIPS and Science Act signed
why_it_matters: Public money returns to semiconductors. Act III's triangle under the name of industrial policy.

event: OpenAI releases ChatGPT
why_it_matters: Adoption figures widely cited from an investment bank estimate rather than a company disclosure.

event: Students for Fair Admissions decided
why_it_matters: Race-conscious admissions held unlawful. What is the credential screening for?

event: Marc Tessier-Lavigne resigns as Stanford president
why_it_matters: Review found manipulation by others in his laboratories and criticised his failure to correct the record.

event: OpenAI board removes its chief executive; reversed within five days
why_it_matters: A governance mechanism designed to constrain commercial logic was tested once and failed.

event: Technology founders seated at the presidential inauguration
why_it_matters: Visibility changes; substance does not. Thiel's roughly $15m to the 2022 Vance campaign is documented in FEC filings.
